predecessors.name: Kingdom of Zimbabwe
predecessors.text: 'located in what is now southwestern Zimbabwe' (Matabeleland North and South with Bulawayo)

successors.name: Rozvi Empire
successors.text: Matabeleland and the Great Zimbabwe core: the kingdom's land at its conquest in c.

ledger.x: c. 1425: Angoche traders open a new gold route that bypasses Great Zimbabwe, and the Torwa dynasty founds the Kingdom of Butua under its first mambo Madabhale. Infobox: 'Established: c. 1425'; 'c. 1425-?: Madabhale'.

c. 1450: the Great Zimbabwe core falls to Butua. The page is silent on a date; the Butua page only has 1922 traditions of a realm 'from Great Zimbabwe to the Makgadikgadi Pan', so 1450 is the researcher's bridge to the Great Zimbabwe dossier's end.

c. 1683: Changamire Dombo conquers Butua. 'Around 1683, the kingdom was conquered by Changamire Dombo, who founded the Rozwi Empire.' 'Certainly by his death in 1696, Changamire controlled all of Butua's territory.'
c. 1683: the Kingdom of Butua ends; infobox 'Conquest by Rozwi Empire: c. 1683', last mambo Madhladhla.

wars.name: Changamire's revolt and the Mutapa-Butua wars
wars.outcome: The Torwa supported a usurper in Mutapa in the 1490s, 'allied the successor, Changamire II, and warred against Mutapa until at least 1512'; no border change is dated.

wars.name: Changamire Dombo's conquest of Butua
wars.outcome: 'Around 1683 Butua was conquered by Changamire Dombo'; by his death in 1696 he controlled all of Butua's territory.

certainty.note: No frontier is described; the extent is a 1922 tradition and the page names no boundary.
